exploration.title: Design Exploration — News Go Wide
exploration.description: An open-ended design exploration using the skill as a creative tool — from spec to multiple outputs in three steps.

steps.title: Prepare the Figma Reference
steps.description: Organize the current design file — summarize the PM spec, identify the existing vertical module (News Events + Related News), and define the design goal: redesign it into a single wide-format module.

images.alt: Figma reference showing current module, current page, and target structure

steps.title: Prompt Claude Code with Context
steps.description: Distill the design goal into a natural language prompt, provide the Figma link, and let Claude fetch the full context via MCP. The skill handles the rest — planning the approach, then generating multiple design directions.

images.alt: Design brief prompt given to Claude

steps.title: Review Multiple Outputs
steps.description: The skill generates a range of design directions — from conservative layouts that respect existing structure to divergent explorations that reimagine the module entirely. Below are two representative examples out of many.

images.alt: Conservative design output — news module expanded to full width
Divergent design output — reimagined news module with list-based layout

captions: ▲ Conservative — faithful to existing page structure
▲ Divergent — reimagined layout with richer visual hierarchy

value.label: Workflow
value.after: Describe intent, AI executes per spec

tips.title: Plan Mode First
tips.description: Use Plan Mode to describe your requirements clearly before execution. This significantly reduces errors and back-and-forth iterations.

tips.title: Work in Steps
tips.description: Break tasks into stages — get the structure right first, then fill in real data later. Incremental progress beats one-shot perfection.

tips.title: Write a Good CLAUDE.md
tips.description: When working on a dedicated project, a well-written CLAUDE.md gives the AI persistent context and dramatically improves output consistency.

tips.title: Accept Minor Variance
tips.description: Small detail differences are normal — not every deviation is a skill bug. Prompts in English tend to yield more predictable results.
